digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate — Pass-2 verify / Pass-3 decide judge reliability measurement
propositions: Self-consistency of the Pass-2/Pass-3 judge over the R5 cohort (G6/E4/T3 findings) must reach Fleiss' κ ≥ 0.6 AND raw agreement ≥ 0.8 across 50 findings with 3 re-judges each, excluding infra-INDETERMINATE verdicts (llm_unavailable or verify_failed flags), or R5 is blocked.

Order-shuffle stability of the gate verdict must reach Fleiss' κ ≥ 0.6 AND raw agreement ≥ 0.8 across 14 plans (≥3 top-level sections) with exactly 3 distinct section-order permutations each, excluding infra-INDETERMINATE verdicts, or R3 is blocked.

E6 drives repeated LLM judge calls (150 agentic Pass-2 votes + 42 full-gate runs) over frozen, committed inputs to measure stochastic stability without circular adjudication, whereas E1's invalidated TP/FP labeling treated gate output as ground truth.

Experiment A freezes and re-runs N=50 findings from runs/adjudication_corpus.jsonl (filtered criterion ∈ {G6,E4,T3}), recording decision from pass3_decide over 3 votes per finding in runs/e6_selfconsistency.jsonl.

Experiment B freezes 14 plans from runs/corpus_sample.json (with ≥3 top-level sections) and generates exactly 3 distinct deterministic section-order permutations (identity + 2 seeded) per plan, re-running the full review_plan entrypoint over a throwaway store clone and recording verdicts in runs/e6_ordershuffle.jsonl.

E6 gates downstream stories R3 and R5: self_consistency.pass → R5 gate, order_shuffle.pass → R3 gate; AC4 revealed 4 archived tickets reducing Exp B to 10/14 surviving plans, landing with order_shuffle.pass=false (κ=0.55, raw=0.70) as an honest R3 blocker.
